facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a low governance reading is that capital returns continue while earnings are lower, and that the redomestication's intellectual property transition could change where value sits in the group; the note obligors have also changed three times since 2022. A debt-funded distribution or acquisition, documentation that moves intellectual property or assets outside the guarantor group, or a distribution restriction that is already close to binding would raise the risk level. Indentures and a proxy statement showing no related-party leakage and an unchanged guarantor structure would confirm the low reading. NCS earnings and the USD 7 million consideration difference are not disclosed; The acquisition's effect on earnings and leverage is not established; Low; Read the Form S-4 and next quarterly report
Backlog and contract duration are not disclosed; Revenue durability is not established; Low; Obtain investor presentations
Redemption of the 2030 notes is not confirmed as completed; Debt after 2026-10-30 is a plan, not a fact; Low; Check the next filing

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Refinancing risk is low because the maturity wall is distant and shrinking. facts.label: Qualitative downside scenario
facts.text: The scenario starts with the Middle East disruption continuing through 2027 while oil prices fall back from their 2026 level. The first operational break would be further declines in drilling-related, wireline, liner hanger and cementation activity in a region that supplies 40.26% of revenue, which pushes down segment EBITDA, as it already has in Well Construction and Completions. Cost of products and services is 69% of revenue, so EBITDA would fall faster than revenue unless headcount and supply costs are cut as quickly as activity falls. The financial transmission is lower operating cash flow, aggravated by a reversal of the receivable collections that supported 2026 and by slower payment from the largest Mexican customer, while dividends and buybacks continue unless the company pauses them. Liquidity would hold: cash of USD 1,161 million (pro forma cash not established) is 78.45% of gross debt, the facility adds USD 599 million, and the company has levers in capital expenditures, the buyback and factoring. Gross leverage would rise above 1.71x and net leverage above 0.37x, and the observable triggers are a fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA at or below USD 254 million, a growing share of receivables owed by the Mexican customer, cash that cannot be repatriated rising above USD 164 million, and any draw on the facility. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress, but the covenant tests cannot be checked without the credit agreement. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Weatherford presents a diversified business profile supported by a small net debt of USD 319 million (USD 321 million pro forma), cash of USD 1,161 million (pro forma cash not established) and a distant maturity wall, but credit quality is constrained by earnings that have fallen about a third from FY2024 and by concentration in a disrupted region. Fundamental credit analysis is complete; top risk: earnings concentration in the Middle East. ## Findings
### Bottom line
Weatherford is lightly levered on a net basis, but creditors are relying on cash rather than earnings, because last-twelve-months EBITDA has fallen about a third since FY2024.
Basis: calculation C61; calculation C62; calculation C72; calculation C71; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_wfrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 68

Net debt was USD 319 million at September 30, 2026 (USD 321 million pro forma for the planned October 30, 2026 redemption of the 2030 notes), or 0.37x last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 867 million, against USD 718 million at FY2024. Gross debt of USD 1,480 million is 1.71x, up from 1.28x, so the improvement came from cash build and repayment, not from earnings. Liquidity is ample, with USD 1,161 million of cash and USD 766 million undrawn.

Basis: calculation C4; calculation C1; calculation C43; calculation C25; calculation C71; calculation C72; calculation C33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16
### Key findings

Leverage is low on a net basis and has risen on a gross basis. Net debt fell by USD 399 million from FY2024 to USD 319 million, because cash rose by USD 245 million to USD 1,161 million and total debt fell by USD 154 million to USD 1,480 million. Against last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 867 million, net leverage is 0.37x and gross leverage 1.71x; on the company's adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,001 million they are 0.32x and 1.48x. Gross leverage was 1.28x at FY2024, so the credit has deleveraged through the numerator while the denominator shrank. ### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is that the company generated USD 379 million of adjusted free cash flow in nine months, that all three agencies hold positive outlooks (Moody's Ba2, S&P BB and Fitch BB), and that management expects a meaningful fourth-quarter ramp in adjusted EBITDA. Fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA that fails to rise from the third quarter's USD 254 million, a further Middle East escalation, or slower collection from the largest Mexican customer would turn the view negative, because cash rather than earnings supports the net leverage. Adjusted EBITDA stabilising near USD 1,001 million with gross leverage below 1.48x would turn it positive.

## Gaps

- The income statement and cash flow lines printed as a dash are shown as not supplied, as the method requires, not as zero; this covers the gain on sale of business, redomestication in nine months 2025, the sale of business, acquisitions, investment sales, borrowings, issuance costs and other financing lines, and the non-cash acquisition items. Severity Low; no action beyond confirming that each dash means nil.

- The quarterly statements fold the loss on extinguishment of debt, the Blue Chip Swap loss, borrowings, issuance costs and investment-sale proceeds into other lines, so those rows are not supplied for the nine-month columns and non-operating items are not like for like between the annual and nine-month columns. Severity Low; no action.

- The company states no unadjusted EBITDA, so EBITDA (Reported) is calculated for every period, and it states no fiscal-year adjusted EBITDA in the sources supplied because no fourth-quarter 2025 release was provided; the FY2024 and FY2025 adjusted figures come from the segment note and the fourth-quarter 2025 figure is the full year less nine months. Severity Low; obtaining the fourth-quarter 2025 release would close it.
- The undrawn committed facility at December 31, 2024 is not supplied, because the commitment in force on that date is not stated. Severity Low; the credit agreement of that date would close it.

- The split of the credit agreement between USD 600 million for borrowing or financial letters of credit and USD 400 million for performance letters of credit is stated only in the annual report; the 2026 reports state the USD 1,000 million total. Severity Medium for liquidity; the credit agreement would confirm the split.

- No source states the security or legal rank of the 2030 notes, the 2033 notes or the finance leases, so they are left out of the debt stack and senior secured debt cannot be separated from the total. Severity Medium; the indentures would close it.

- The maturity table is drawn at December 31, 2025 because no later schedule is printed, and the amount due in 2030 includes the 2030 notes that are to be redeemed. Completion of the redemption on October 30, 2026, and the accrued interest paid with it, are neither confirmed nor stated. Severity Medium; the next filing would close it.
- The remaining principal of the 2030 notes at December 31, 2024 is given only to the nearest hundred million, so total principal at that date is not stated exactly. Severity Low; no action.

- Covenant levels are stated, but the definitions, the company's calculated ratios and any headroom are not, so covenant capacity is not calculated here. Severity Medium; the credit agreement and a compliance certificate would close it.

- The company reclassified some 2025 interim amounts to the 2026 presentation without stating them, so last-twelve-months figures that combine an annual 2025 figure with a reclassified nine-month 2025 figure carry a small basis risk. Severity Low; no action.
- Pension figures are at December 31, 2025 only and the legal contingencies note gives no amounts, so both are carried without a 2026 update. Severity Low; the next annual report would update them.
- The dividend amount uses the shares outstanding on October 15, 2026; the share count at the record date is not stated. Severity Low; no action.
- Cash interest paid is lumpy because coupons are semiannual, so last-twelve-months cash interest cover can move with payment timing. Severity Low; no action.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Weatherford is a listed, diversified oilfield services company with no sponsor or controlling shareholder named in the supplied sources, so creditors face cyclical and structural risk rather than owner-extraction risk.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-12-31_wfrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99; Source readiness (CP-0)

The changes that matter are the USD 128 million NCS Multistage acquisition completed on September 1, 2026, the planned move of the parent from Ireland to Delaware in the fourth quarter, and the redemption of the 2030 notes. Shareholder returns of USD 113 million in nine months were covered by free cash flow. Governance risk is assessed as low on documented behaviour only, because no indenture, credit agreement or proxy statement was supplied to test legal capacity or control rights.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C21; calculation C20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4
### Key findings

No owner is shown to control the company, so owner-driven leverage or extraction risk is not evidenced. The company is listed on Nasdaq, and the only holder the filings name is the largest shareholder of the acquired business, which received 0.49% of the shares outstanding in the NCS transaction. The proxy statement that would list major holders, director independence and related-party dealings was not supplied, so control rights and related-party leakage are not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-K_2025-12-31_wfrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99; calculation C19

The business is diversified by product line but concentrated by region. Over nine months of 2026, Drilling and Evaluation produced 27.74% of revenue, Well Construction and Completions 39.00%, Production and Intervention 27.24% and non-core integrated services 6.03%, and services were 61.35% of the total. The Middle East, North Africa and Asia region supplied 40.26% of revenue after falling by USD 191 million from the prior nine months, which the company attributes to the Iran conflict; the United States at 14% and Russia at 9% are the only other countries near a tenth of revenue.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C9; calculation C11; calculation C16

Customer concentration is moderate, but the largest Mexican customer matters for cash collection. No customer exceeded 10% of 2025 revenue, though the largest customer, in Mexico, was 10% of 2024 revenue and has a history of late payment; it was 14% of net receivables at September 30, 2026, down from 24% at the end of 2025. The company says those balances are not in dispute, so the exposure is collection timing rather than loss, but this customer has at times used third-party financial institutions to pay the company's receivables.

The NCS acquisition is small against the balance sheet, at 2.40% of total assets, and was paid mainly in shares. Total consideration of USD 128 million was settled with shares valued at USD 101 million, USD 13 million of cash net of cash acquired and USD 7 million of assumed equity awards, and it brought tangible assets of USD 150 million and USD 34 million of noncontrolling interests. The sources do not give NCS revenue or EBITDA and do not explain a USD 7 million gap between the stated components and the total, so the effect on earnings and leverage is not established.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C24; calculation C25; calculation C26; calculation C27

The move from Ireland to Delaware is the main structural change, and its creditor effect is not yet documented. Shareholders approved it on September 3, 2026 after an earlier Texas proposal failed to obtain the required approval despite more than 60% support; it still needs Irish High Court sanction and is expected in the fourth quarter. The company expects USD 20 million to USD 30 million of annual cash savings from 2027 and spent USD 30 million on it in nine months, but a planned intellectual property transition is still being evaluated for accounting and tax implications, and the sources do not say which group entities would hold the intellectual property afterwards.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-06-30_wfrd-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-03-31_wfrd-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 12; EX-99.1_2026-10-20_a2026-q3ex991earningsrelea.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C28

Changes to the note obligors look neutral on their face but cannot be confirmed without the indentures. Since 2022 the company has added subsidiaries as co-issuers of the notes three times and released their guarantees, most recently on September 25, 2026 for a Texas subsidiary on the 2033 notes. A co-issuer is directly liable, so the change need not weaken claims, but guarantor coverage, ranking and any release conditions cannot be checked.

Shareholder returns are material but covered by cash flow. Dividends of USD 59 million and buybacks of USD 54 million over nine months total USD 113 million, which is 31.22% of free cash flow of USD 362 million after capital expenditures; the quarterly dividend per share is 10.00% above 2025, and USD 246 million of the buyback authorisation remains. Returns are discretionary, and the notes and credit agreement restrict distributions in terms the sources do not give.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-K_2025-12-31_wfrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_wfrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C21; calculation C20; calculation C22; calculation C23

Reporting quality supports monitoring, with two disclosure limits. The annual statements carry an unqualified KPMG opinion, disclosure controls were assessed effective at September 30, 2026 while NCS is integrated, and the third-quarter earnings release came a day before the quarterly report. Legal contingencies are described without amounts, and the 2025 comparatives were reclassified without stating the changes.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a low governance reading is that capital returns continue while earnings are lower, and that the redomestication's intellectual property transition could change where value sits in the group; the note obligors have also changed three times since 2022. A debt-funded distribution or acquisition, documentation that moves intellectual property or assets outside the guarantor group, or a distribution restriction that is already close to binding would raise the risk level. Indentures and a proxy statement showing no related-party leakage and an unchanged guarantor structure would confirm the low reading.
### Limitations

- No proxy statement was supplied, so the ownership register and board independence cannot be checked; the low governance reading rests on documented behaviour and would change if a controlling or activist holder or related-party payments appeared.

- No indenture or credit agreement text was supplied, so legal capacity for distributions, liens, asset transfers and guarantor releases is untested; this keeps the governance reading to willingness evidence and could change it.

- The intellectual property transition inside the redomestication is described only as under evaluation, so the conclusion that the structure change is neutral for creditors depends on documents that are not in the sources.
- NCS revenue, EBITDA and pro forma effects are not disclosed, so the conclusion that the acquisition is small rests on its price against the group and not on its earnings contribution.
- Backlog and contract duration are not disclosed, so the diversification conclusion describes revenue mix and not revenue durability.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The NCS Multistage acquisition was agreed on May 31, 2026 and completed on September 1, 2026 for total consideration of USD 128 million, paid in shares, cash and assumed equity awards, and NCS is now a wholly owned subsidiary that adds completions technology and unconventional-market exposure. No new debt was issued in 2026 through the latest filing; the last issue was the USD 1,200 million of 2033 notes on October 6, 2025, which refinanced most of the 2030 notes, and on October 20, 2026 the company gave notice to redeem the remaining USD 236 million of the 2030 notes on October 30, 2026 from cash. The parent's redomestication from Ireland to Delaware, approved by shareholders on September 3, 2026, is expected in the fourth quarter and is not a financing transaction.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Weatherford can service and refinance its debt from cash, with net debt of USD 319 million (USD 321 million pro forma for the October 30, 2026 redemption of the 2030 notes), but earnings, down about a third from FY2024, are the weak side.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3

Cash of USD 1,161 million covers the USD 264 million of debt now classified as current 4.40 times, and no bond matures before 2033 once the 2030 notes are redeemed; Financial foundation states no pro forma cash after the redemption, so cash after it is not established. The primary downside path is a prolonged Middle East disruption that lowers EBITDA further while receivable collections reverse and shareholder returns continue, which would raise gross leverage from 1.71x but would take a long time to threaten liquidity.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C26; calculation C27; calculation C28; calculation C7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16
### Key findings

Leverage is low on a net basis, and the pro forma figures do not change that. Net debt at September 30, 2026 was USD 319 million, or 0.37x last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 867 million; pro forma for the October 30, 2026 redemption of the 2030 notes it is USD 321 million and 0.37x, and pro forma for the December 3, 2026 dividend payment it is USD 338.93 million and 0.39x. Gross debt of USD 1,480 million is 1.71x, up from 1.28x at FY2024 because EBITDA fell by more than debt did; on the company's adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,001 million the net and gross figures are 0.32x and 1.48x.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16

Earnings are the weakest dimension and carry the downside. Last-twelve-months reported EBITDA is 32.32% below FY2024 and adjusted EBITDA 27.57% below, on revenue 14.95% lower at USD 4,689 million. The Middle East, North Africa and Asia region, 40.26% of revenue, fell by USD 191 million over nine months because of the Iran conflict, and Well Construction and Completions margin fell to 23.91% from 27.18%, while Production and Intervention margin rose to 21.27%. No backlog or contract duration is disclosed, so revenue visibility beyond the company's expectation of an improving fourth quarter is not established.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C18; calculation C19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29

Cash flow quality improved in 2026 but is helped by receivable collections. Free cash flow after capital expenditures was USD 362 million over nine months against USD 233 million, which is 50.99% of adjusted EBITDA against 30.03%, and capital expenditures were 4.15% of revenue, inside the company's 3% to 5% range. USD 186 million of operating cash flow came from receivable collections, so the figure overstates the repeatable level; against that, factoring proceeds fell by USD 215 million, so the cash flow does not rest on selling receivables.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C20; calculation C21; calculation C22; calculation C23; calculation C24; calculation C25; calculation C44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32

Liquidity covers every scheduled obligation, with two qualifications. Cash of USD 1,161 million (pro forma cash after the redemption is not established), of which USD 164 million cannot be immediately repatriated, plus USD 599 million of the undrawn facility that can be borrowed, gives USD 1,760 million against gross debt of USD 1,480 million, or 1.19x; USD 167 million of the facility is for performance letters of credit only, and USD 531 million of letters of credit and USD 534 million of surety bonds could be called. Covenant levels are stated, but their definitions and the company's calculated ratios are not, so covenant headroom is not established here.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C26; calculation C32; calculation C33; calculation C30; calculation C31; calculation C34; calculation C45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34

Refinancing risk is low because the maturity wall is distant and shrinking. The 2033 notes carry USD 1,200 million of principal, the credit agreement runs to September 18, 2030 once the 2030 notes are gone, and the annual report schedules only USD 29 million of maturities in 2026, USD 20 million in 2027, USD 9 million in 2028 and USD 4 million in 2029, all finance leases. Redeeming USD 236 million of 2030 notes from cash saves about USD 20 million of annual cash interest; no filing yet confirms completion.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C35; calculation C36; calculation C37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; EX-99.1_2026-10-20_a2026-q3ex991earningsrelea.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_wfrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 86

Governance and financial policy add little risk on the evidence available. Business & governance names no sponsor or controlling holder and rates sponsor and governance risk low on documented behaviour; shareholder returns of USD 113 million are 31.22% of nine-month free cash flow, and the 2025 refinancing and the planned redemption reduce debt. The open questions are the intellectual property transition inside the move to Delaware and three changes of note obligors since 2022, which cannot be tested without the indentures.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C38; calculation C47; calculation C20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16

Customer and country concentration is the second-order risk. The largest Mexican customer is 14% of net receivables and has a record of late payment, and Russia is 9% of revenue and holds USD 128 million of cash. At these levels they are collection and trapped-cash risks and not solvency risks, but they sit in the same regions as the disruption that is lowering earnings.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C41; calculation C42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32

The outlook is for gradual recovery with the Middle East timing uncertain. The company expects activity to improve through the rest of 2026 in North America and Latin America and from the NCS acquisition, and a meaningful fourth-quarter ramp in adjusted EBITDA, and it calls the pace of Middle East recovery the main uncertainty. For scale, a fourth quarter at the fourth-quarter 2025 level of USD 291 million would be 14.57% above the third quarter's USD 254 million; WTI averaged USD 84.98 over nine months against USD 67.40 a year earlier, a price rise that has not lifted Middle East activity.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; EX-99.1_2026-10-20_a2026-q3ex991earningsrelea.htm.jsonl, page 3; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C39; calculation C40
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that net leverage has fallen to 0.37x (0.37x pro forma for the October 30, 2026 redemption), that nine-month free cash flow was USD 362 million, that each agency holds a positive outlook, and that management still expects a meaningful fourth-quarter recovery. A fourth quarter that fails to lift adjusted EBITDA above the third quarter's USD 254 million, a reversal of the USD 186 million of receivable collections, or a rise in the largest Mexican customer's 14% share of receivables would turn the view negative. Adjusted EBITDA holding near USD 1,001 million with free cash flow conversion near 50.99% would turn it positive.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C6; calculation C20; calculation C48; calculation C24; calculation C41; calculation C11; calculation C21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; EX-99.1_2026-10-20_a2026-q3ex991earningsrelea.htm.jsonl, page 3
### Limitations

- No indenture or credit agreement was supplied, so the low refinancing-risk conclusion rests on maturities and covenant levels as the filings summarise them, and guarantor coverage, ranking and covenant headroom are untested.
- No peer, market price or rating agency report was supplied, so the credit view is absolute: it does not say how the profile compares with other oilfield services issuers or how the notes trade.

- The fourth-quarter recovery the company expects is not quantified and its Middle East timing is open, so the conclusion that earnings are the weakest dimension could move either way within a quarter.
- Receivable collections and factoring are reported only as cash flow lines, so the repeatable level of free cash flow is bounded, not measured.
- The 2030 notes redemption and the dividend payment are plans after the latest filing, and Financial foundation states no pro forma cash, so liquidity after October 30, 2026 is not established.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Net debt is small against earnings: net debt of USD 319 million (USD 321 million pro forma) is 0.37x last-twelve-months EBITDA (0.37x pro forma), so a further decline in EBITDA would raise leverage but not threaten the debt service capacity of a group that holds USD 1,161 million of cash (pro forma cash not established). The company controls its largest discretionary uses of cash: capital expenditures are 4.15% of revenue against a guided range of 3% to 5%, and USD 246 million of buyback authorisation can be left unused, which gives a means to protect cash in a downturn. The business spans three segments and four regions, and Production and Intervention margin rose to 21.27% while Well Construction and Completions fell, so the weakness is not uniform. The debt profile has no bond maturity before 2033 once the 2030 notes are redeemed, and the company is retiring them from cash.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C6; calculation C26; calculation C23; calculation C19; calculation C18; calculation C36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38

Weaknesses. Earnings fell by about a third from FY2024 because a region that supplies 40.26% of revenue was disrupted, and the company gives no backlog to show when earnings recover. Part of the 2026 cash flow is receivable collections of USD 186 million that will not repeat, so reported free cash flow is not a run-rate. The largest Mexican customer, 14% of net receivables, pays late, and USD 164 million of cash cannot be immediately repatriated. Ownership and legal documents were not supplied, so control rights, guarantor coverage and covenant headroom are unknown, and the planned move to Delaware carries an intellectual property transition whose creditor effect is undisclosed.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C12; calculation C17; calculation C24; calculation C41; calculation C32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32

Business risk in credit terms. The industry has four large competitors and customers that are mostly national and international oil companies, so pricing and technology pressure come from both sides, and spending follows oil prices and rig counts. Political and trade developments matter directly: the Iran conflict has cut Middle East activity, Russia carries sanctions and nationalisation risk, and tariffs are described as a possible cost. Technology and the energy transition are a long-run factor for the products and the credit, but the filings give no evidence that either is a primary driver over the debt's life.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wfrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_wfrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Business model, margin resilience and cash conversion

The business sells services and equipment across the well life cycle, with services at 61.35% of nine-month revenue, so revenue follows customer drilling and workover activity and not long-term contracts, and the filings give no backlog. Cost of products and services is 69% of revenue, headcount reductions lowered personnel costs and restructuring charges fell to USD 28 million from USD 51 million, which shows some cost flexibility, so margins can be defended under moderate volume pressure but, as an analyst judgement, not under a deep fall in activity. Capital intensity is moderate, working capital is the main swing factor in cash flow, and the receivable position of a Mexican customer with a history of late payment is the observed pressure point.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the tailwinds are higher oil prices, higher worldwide rig counts, the NCS completions portfolio, the end of the 2030 notes' cash interest and, from 2027, the USD 20 million to USD 30 million of annual cash savings the company expects from the redomestication. The headwinds are the Middle East disruption, the new tariffs the company describes as a possible cost, the ongoing Russia exposure, and the cost of integrating NCS. Over three to five years the filings point to energy security and offshore and deepwater spending as structural supports, which is management language and is not evidenced by contract data in the sources.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; EX-99.1_2026-10-20_a2026-q3ex991earningsrelea.htm.jsonl, page 6; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Qualitative downside scenario

The scenario starts with the Middle East disruption continuing through 2027 while oil prices fall back from their 2026 level. The first operational break would be further declines in drilling-related, wireline, liner hanger and cementation activity in a region that supplies 40.26% of revenue, which pushes down segment EBITDA, as it already has in Well Construction and Completions. Cost of products and services is 69% of revenue, so EBITDA would fall faster than revenue unless headcount and supply costs are cut as quickly as activity falls. The financial transmission is lower operating cash flow, aggravated by a reversal of the receivable collections that supported 2026 and by slower payment from the largest Mexican customer, while dividends and buybacks continue unless the company pauses them. Liquidity would hold: cash of USD 1,161 million (pro forma cash not established) is 78.45% of gross debt, the facility adds USD 599 million, and the company has levers in capital expenditures, the buyback and factoring. Gross leverage would rise above 1.71x and net leverage above 0.37x, and the observable triggers are a fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA at or below USD 254 million, a growing share of receivables owed by the Mexican customer, cash that cannot be repatriated rising above USD 164 million, and any draw on the facility. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress, but the covenant tests cannot be checked without the credit agreement.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C17; calculation C26; calculation C29; calculation C30; calculation C7; calculation C6; calculation C39; calculation C41; calculation C32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32
### Overall credit view

Overall, Weatherford presents a diversified business profile supported by a small net debt of USD 319 million (USD 321 million pro forma), cash of USD 1,161 million (pro forma cash not established) and a distant maturity wall, but credit quality is constrained by earnings that have fallen about a third from FY2024 and by concentration in a disrupted region. Cash-flow durability is adequate and not strong, because USD 186 million of 2026 operating cash flow was receivable collections. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on an EBITDA recovery before the credit agreement matures in 2030 and on its legal terms, which were not supplied. The primary downside path is a prolonged Middle East disruption with collections reversing. Further analysis would require the indentures and credit agreement, the proxy statement, peer and market data, backlog, and the company's covenant calculations. Fundamental credit analysis is complete; top risk: earnings concentration in the Middle East.
